messages:
ash: quick q — proposal to add an ephemeral operator override for automatic fallback policies. toggle in console or API that lasts N minutes and is auditable. use case: urgent rollout QA where we want a temporary, reversible bypass without changing the canonical policy :thinking:

mira: do you mean a one-off 'hold' that prevents fallback from triggering, or an 'force-fallback' button? both have different risk profiles.

ash: mostly 'hold'/pause for specific route or rollout id. example: canary spiking false positives, ops wants to pause autofallback for 10m while investigating. not a policy change.

sahil: important: must emit strong audit events, with identity + TTL + justification text. ops teams will need to query who did what. also need RBAC — only certain roles can hold overrides.

joanne: UX idea: in route detail show small pill "Active Overrides (1)" with start, expires, author, reason. clicking expands to timeline + link to audit log. quick revoke button.

ash: thank you. for API we'd need an endpoint like: POST /v1/rollouts/:id/overrides { action: "pause_autofallback", ttl_secs: 600, reason: "investigating 500 spike" }

ryan: debate: enforcement point — control-plane-level flag vs runtime router-level token. If control-plane only, router may still trigger fallback during propagation lag. runtime token is safer but requires router auth checks + slight perf cost.

sahil: agree. prefer token that routers validate so decision is immediate. token can be short-lived signed JWT with policy id and exp. routers already verify signature on config blobs.

mira: what about audit retention? we need minimum 365d for compliance customers. storing full payload in event log is fine but UI should show truncated reason + link to raw audit.

ash: also want telemetry emitted: override.start, override.expire, override.revoke, override.enforcement_skipped (if router unable to apply). tag metrics with rollout_id, route, actor_id.

sahil: add sanity: telemetry should include pre/post fallback attempt counts during override windows to help owners decide if override was useful. low-cardinality keys only.

ryan: edge case: multiple overlapping overrides from different operators. UX should show prioritized stack — latest wins, but we record history. maybe disallow two active 'pause' overrides on same target if durations overlap?

joanne: disallowing could annoy teams. better: allow multiple but display owner & expiration; revoke should only remove the one you created unless you have escalation privilege.

ash: thought on UI controls: quick dropdown for preset durations (10m, 30m, 2h) + custom TTL. Require a reason (min 15 chars) and checkbox "I confirm this is temporary" to slow accidental usage.

mira: +1. also surface SLO impact estimate inline (small card) so you know roughly how many requests may degrade if you pause autofallback. compute by sampling recent fallback triggers.

ops-bot: audit:event created -> type:override.create actor:ash target:rollout_42 action:pause_autofallback ttl:600 reason:"investigating 500 spike" id:ovr_20231101_01

sahil: security: ensure overrides respect customer scoping. private deployments should enforce customer-local policies and do not accept cross-tenant overrides. console should gray out controls for non-admins.

ash: implementation checklist proposal: 1) API endpoint + schema 2) signed runtime token flows 3) audit event stream + retention 4) console pill + revoke UX 5) RBAC checks + escalation paths 6) telemetry counters & SLO impact estimate

ryan: i'll take tokens + router integration, sahil can lead audit + retention, joanne on UX, ash + mira on API/console wiring.

mira: one more thing — rollback automation: if override expires and immediate fallback triggers are now allowed, we should optionally auto-snooze for an extra X mins if the operator checked "extend if errors persist". dangerous but handy. default: off.

joanne: will mock that in the next design pass. UX will hide advanced checkbox under "advanced options" so basic users don't accidentally enable it.

ash: can someone add this to the rollout spec doc and create a short RFC? i'd like a small demo before next oncall rotation.

sahil: created a draft RFC in docs/rollouts/overrides.md (WIP).

ops-bot: reminder: please include unit tests for token validation and a feature flag to gate rollout. :white_check_mark:

ryan: thanks — will sync after lunch.

ash: cool, thanks everyone. follow-ups: joanne will post mockups, ryan & sahil will ping when infra PRs are up.

mira: tagging this for product review next Tues. :calendar:

ash: closing thread for now. feel free to continue replies here if something pops up.
